h1: The 6 Best Blenders Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six blenders under $100, from full pitchers to personal cups, compared on wattage, capacity, jar material and fit.
summary: The Ninja Professional BL610 is our top blender under $100 for most kitchens. The Nutri-Blender Pro suits single servings, the UltraCrush adds manual speed dials, the Black+Decker PowerCrush brings a glass jar, the Ninja Fit fits tight counters, and the Hamilton Beach is the budget glass option.
intro: Wattage sells blenders, but jar size and blade design decide what you can actually make. A 1000W motor in a 72 oz pitcher and a 700W personal cup are different tools, even when both cost under $100.

We ranked six blenders from their listings on motor power, capacity, jar material and controls. All sit at or below the $50-100 bucket, so the choice comes down to what you blend most and how much counter you have.

products.name: Ninja Professional Blender, 1000W, Total Crushing Tech, 72oz Pitcher, BL610
products.verdict: One dependable full-pitcher blender for most kitchens.
products.description:
The Ninja Professional BL610 has a 1000W motor, a 72 oz pitcher and Total Crushing blade technology, in the $50-100 bracket.

It wins because the big pitcher and 1000W cover family-size batches. The UltraCrush below matches the wattage and capacity, and the personal blenders trade pitcher size for portability.

It suits anyone wanting one reliable pitcher blender. The caveat is its size, since a 72 oz pitcher needs counter or cabinet room.

products.name: Ninja Nutri-Blender Pro with Auto iQ, 1100PW, (2) 24oz Cups, BN401
products.verdict: Single-serve smoothies with presets and two to-go cups.
products.description:
The Nutri-Blender Pro has 1100 peak watts, two 24 oz to-go cups and Auto-iQ preset programs, at $50-100.

It ranks second because it trades the pitcher for cups. Against the Nutri-Plus below, it has the higher peak watts and presets.

It suits single-serve smoothie drinkers. The caveat is that 24 oz cups cap each batch.

products.name: Ninja UltraCrush Professional Blender, 1000W, 72oz Pitcher, 3 Speeds, BP201
products.verdict: Same pitcher and wattage, with three manual speeds.
products.description:
The UltraCrush has a 1000W motor, a 72 oz pitcher and 3 manual speed settings, in the $50-100 bracket.

It ranks third because its core specs match the BL610 above, so the only real difference is the physical speed dial. That is the draw for buyers who dislike presets.

It suits cooks who want direct control. The caveat is that nothing here beats the top pick on raw capability.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer manual speed dials.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER PowerCrush Multi-Function Blender, 6-Cup Glass Jar, 4 Speeds
products.verdict: A scratch-resistant glass jar at a lower price.
products.description:
The PowerCrush has a 6-cup glass jar, 4 speed settings and a multi-function PowerCrush blade, in the $25-50 bracket.

It ranks fourth because it gives no wattage in its listing, so we cannot rank its power against the Ninjas above. The glass jar is the selling point over plastic.

It suits buyers who want glass for durability. The caveat is the missing motor spec.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want glass over plastic.
products.skipIf: You want a stated high wattage.

products.name: Ninja Fit Compact Personal Blender, 700W, (2) 16oz Cups, QB3001SS
products.verdict: A compact personal blender for dorms and desks.
products.description:
The Ninja Fit has a 700W motor and two 16 oz cups in a compact personal-blender body, at $50-100.

It ranks fifth because 700W and 16 oz cups are the smallest in the Ninja lineup here. It is the best choice when counter space is tight.

It suits dorms or small desks. The caveat is the small cup capacity.

products.name: Hamilton Beach Power Elite Blender with Wave Action System
products.verdict: A budget blender with a glass jar and Wave Action.
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach Power Elite has a glass jar, multiple speed settings and the Wave Action mixing system, in the $25-50 bracket.

It ranks last because its listing gives neither wattage nor capacity. It undercuts others on price while keeping glass.

It suits budget-first buyers. The caveat is the thin spec sheet.

whatMatters.detail: Watts measure motor power. It matters for crushing ice and frozen fruit. Check whether the listing says peak watts or continuous watts.
This is how much a jar holds. It matters for batch size. Compare ounces, such as 72 oz versus 16 oz.
Glass resists scratches and plastic is lighter. It matters for durability and weight. Check the spec list for the jar material.
Presets automate and manual speeds give control. It matters for habits. Check whether the listing names presets or speed settings.
Bigger pitchers take space. It matters in small kitchens. Compare the form factor, pitcher or personal cup.

faq.a: It helps with ice and frozen fruit. For soft ingredients, less may do.
Peak watts, as on the Nutri-Blender Pro, describe a short burst. Prefer the rated figure when comparing.
Glass resists scratches but weighs more, as with the Black+Decker.

faq.q: How do I use a personal cup blender?
faq.a: Fill the cup, attach the blade and blend, then drink from the same cup.
Rinse promptly, and check the listing for dishwasher-safe parts.
Check the manual. Listings here do not state hot-liquid use.

finalTake: The Ninja Professional BL610 is the best blender under $100 for most kitchens. Choose the Nutri-Blender Pro for smoothies and the Ninja Fit for small counters. The Black+Decker is the pick if you want glass.
